analysis.analysis: An aggregator of provenance is composed with its sources and partners right and its own state left out: a reader cannot tell from the composition that the project ended in 2020. The grain is the project's own description; the record's lifecycle field carries what the composition does not.
analysis.d: MAPPING MANUSCRIPT MIGRATIONS, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts.' Scale ('over 215,000 historical manuscripts'), partners (Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS, Aalto) and funding (the Trans-Atlantic Platform's Digging into Data Challenge), and the merged sources (the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue') as a linked open data knowledge graph, queryable through the portal and LDF.fi. Six cards: the GitHub page, the Journal of Open Humanities Data (2020), EADH, the University of San Diego, the Zenodo record of the knowledge graph, Goldsmiths Research Online.

Scale ('over 215,000 historical manuscripts'), partners (Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS, Aalto) and funding (the Trans-Atlantic Platform's Digging into Data Challenge), and the merged sources (the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue') as a linked open data knowledge graph, queryable through the portal and LDF.fi. findings: THE PROJECT HELD. Partners and funder are the record's; the aggregation of three databases into linked open data is its self-description. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the entity pages it saved.

THE COUNT. 'over 215,000' follows the San Diego card ('more than 215,000 medieval'); the record's white-paper figures are 217,700 manuscripts and other entities in the portal and 262,000 source records combined.

ONE SOURCE COARSENED. The record names the three sources as 'the Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts, Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries, and Bibale'; 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue' drops Oxford from the name of the Bodleian's catalogue.
WHAT IS NOT GIVEN. The project's term (funded 2017–2020; the data maintained after) and the licence (CC BY-NC 4.0) are absent; the Zenodo copy of the dataset appears as a card.
analysis.mt: MAPPING MANUSCRIPT MIGRATIONS ON THE OVERVIEW — THE FOUR PARTNERS AND DIGGING INTO DATA RIGHT; 'OVER 215,000' MANUSCRIPTS; THE OXFORD CATALOGUE GIVEN AS 'THE MEDIEVAL MANUSCRIPTS CATALOGUE'; THE PROJECT'S END IN 2020 AND ITS LICENCE UNSAID

[QUERENT] Mapping Manuscript Migrations

[SYSTEM] Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) is an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVhiimUeIBTse6JWvsBmsU24mXHagnL86aMRmjbyJGZCOFD7-vYmw7Ljh9-LM1mteFS0mFmQ97CFH0vmB35jt2Ad7eFpcK_bEDkjkV3eA0vq8GMSI5jwd1SotonlHnHSTgVSRLm01Qlg)]
Core Overview

* Objective & Scale: Traces the global journey of over 215,000 historical manuscripts from their creation to modern collections, enabling analysis from individual manuscript lifecycles to macro-level trade and collection trends. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV9BINJaAaGTfKDbBNmIRJ8cjfAGJ4bc3FUVbxxVTQp1CvkYLWSjtY0RtfuBiDAACnQj_Hz5fhY9oY-qRdz_KsGbIRZA9sRcYv3ufQiSTBYFJ7ueTWnLg4HYYasLzXPI7jXDRrVacPGdIpsdyq1rBBk7Gn), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVFVwnPxxYhckZeDS2BUD8aXaAi4K17ZolyQzC40Avsmeq-Qhd7QK4kRCYvWBp2ZxFe2hNdBaTANODbzmEc3HxYg3_DhqfmNx99Q2x6O264S_L09cnDV1aqq9htfwr3M8mVrLtnU23rpOh_w), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVhiimUeIBTse6JWvsBmsU24mXHagnL86aMRmjbyJGZCOFD7-vYmw7Ljh9-LM1mteFS0mFmQ97CFH0vmB35jt2Ad7eFpcK_bEDkjkV3eA0vq8GMSI5jwd1SotonlHnHSTgVSRLm01Qlg)]
* Partners & Funding: A collaboration between the University of Pennsylvania, University of Oxford, Institut de recherche et d'histoire des textes (IRHT-CNRS), and Aalto University, funded by the Trans-Atlantic Platform’s Digging into Data Challenge. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVmBjuFIT9rydIIXbC770wmUabUPGoHPr4yK-vGLkAJZ06_B8qUFNMyGvUVGtvXd6fSouJbWngKjR8F0BFEmx7Ivw-39uRZy58qcy6tc8s7f7t1IC1Z6noyh70B3S4D8o), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky)]

Unified Datasets & Access
The project merges records from the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, and the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue into a Linked Open Data knowledge graph. Researchers can explore and query the data via the project's semantic portal and LDF.fi.
